feedback: Accepted — the reachable behavior of this RM is correct and safe for the task; two provably unreachable transitions should be cleaned up but are inert. Core checks pass: (1) Structure/format — REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION headers all present in the paper format; FINAL_STATES: u4 is nonempty, declared among STATES, and reached exactly on target_picked_up, which is the episode-terminating event. (2) Ordered transition coverage — the ball-first ordering (blocker_moved → has_door_key → door_open → target_picked_up) maps to u0→u1→u2→u3→u4 with dense bounded rewards 0.1/0.1/0.3/1.0; the key-first ordering is covered by u0→u2 plus the explicit key_lost regressions (u2→u0 with ball unmoved, u2→u1 with ball moved, both −0.3), so the task's soft constraint 'do not drop the key while the door is closed' is implemented as a net-negative detour (key-first totals 1.3 vs 1.5 for ball-first). (3) Persistent/event distinctions — key_lost is correctly treated as a one-step event: the regression/penalty fires only at the drop step and nothing lingers; blocker_moved reversion (ball dropped back in front of the door) is absorbed by else self-loops without spurious state regression, which is right since ball reversion is not a task regression. (4) Reward safety — no positive farming: every drop-and-repick-key cycle nets −0.2 or worse, door_open cannot be re-earned (the door cannot be re-shut), the +0.2/+0.1 asymmetry is consistent, and the necessary drop of the key after the door is open (example trace step 19) correctly incurs no penalty. Every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant or infeasible combinations. (5) Reachability — u1–u4 are all reachable and u4 is reachable from every state; no dead ends. Flaws to note (inert, recommend removal): (a) (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key & !door_open) → u2 (+0.2) is unreachable — the two conditions arise from two different pickup steps, the agent holds one object, and the RM always exits u0 on whichever occurs first, so this conjunction can never be the first event in u0; (b) (u3, key_lost) → u3 (−0.3) is unreachable — key_lost entails ¬door_open by definition (the constraint list states key_lost and door_open never hold together) and the door cannot be toggled shut, so key_lost can in fact only ever fire while in u2, where the existing −0.3 transitions already give complete coverage; a penalty here would also have expressed the wrong intent, since dropping the key with the door open is a required step to free the hands for the box. Deleting both entries leaves the induced reward signal unchanged.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented with no undeclared extras, none missing, and none unused. Alignment and fidelity checks: (1) has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented truth conditions exactly (carrying a key matching a door's color found by grid scan; any open door; carrying a box whose color matches the mission string), covering the declared mission-target API rather than a hardcoded color. (2) blocker_moved reproduces the reference reading: it anchors on the (single) door found by scan and checks the cell at (x-1, y) for a ball, which is the documented start-side front cell (dx-1, dy); a picked-up ball is off-grid so it counts as moved, and the cell is re-read every step, so dropping the ball back there turns it false again - correct condition, non-latch semantics. The x > 0 guard keeps the neighbor lookup in bounds and cannot suppress a real blocker since the shared-wall door always has x >= 1. (3) key_lost correctly implements the event: previous_valuation['has_door_key'] true and current has_door_key false and current door_open false, so it fires for exactly one step and cannot co-occur with has_door_key or door_open; it reads episode_memory read-only with a harmless falsy guard and never mutates env or memory. Persistent propositions use only current state; the event uses only the read-only previous-valuation snapshot as permitted. API scope is respected: only grid.get/width/height, carrying (type, color), door is_open, mission, and previous_valuation are used; empty cells are guarded with 'cell is not None' before attribute reads; object classes are not imported; there are no imports, actions, side effects, or mutations; syntax is valid Python and all generator expressions follow the documented scan idiom with correct short-circuit ordering.
